newsitem.title: CANADA: Murder inquiry into Bre-X geologist death - paper.
newsitem.headline: Murder inquiry into Bre-X geologist death - paper.

text.p: Indonesian police have launched a murder investigation into the death of Michael de Guzman, former deputy chief geologist for Bre-X Minerals Ltd, the Globe and Mail newspaper reported Saturday.

Brigadier-General Ahwil Luthan, a senior official with Indonesia's National Census Bureau, told the newspaper that the case is being reopened and the chief of police has discussed the probe with the Philippines' ambassador.
"Until today we thought maybe it was suicide," Luthan was quoted as saying. "But now we have a lot of questions. We are still open to the possibility it was murder."
De Guzman, a Filipino, plunged from a helicopter on March 26 into the Indonesian jungle near Bre-X's Busang gold project.

Busang was once touted as the biggest gold find of the century, but independent auditors last week concluded it contained virtually no gold. They said the Bre-X test samples had been tampered with on a massive scale. Canadian police have begun an investigation into the affair in an attempt to determine who was responsible.
Luthan told the Globe that the probe was focusing on a few key company officials but he would not say who. He said de Guzman was a target of the investigation because of his suspicious death.
Indonesian authorities have also detained two Filipino geologists for questioning at the Busang site, the Globe said.

Cesar Puspos, project manager at Busang, is believed to have key information but he left Indonesia several weeks ago. Luthan said he had not been located and relatives of Puspos in the Philippines told the Globe that he was traveling to Australia.
Luthan said investigators especially want to interview former Bre-X chief geologist John Felderhoff who is in the Cayman Islands. Felderhoff has denied being involved in any fraud.

The Financial Post newspaper said Saturday that forensic investigators from Price Waterhouse questioned Bre-X geologists in Indonesia on Friday. The firm was hired by Bre-X President David Walsh to unravel the affair.
The Toronto Star newspaper reported Saturday that Walsh hired the investigators in late April to look into possible fraud while he publicly insisted tests would confirm a Busang gold find.

The Star said Bre-X retained Forensic Investigative Associates and Price Waterhouse on April 22 to review operations in Jakarta and Busang. The hiring was revealed only after independent auditors released their findings on Busang a week ago.

The Financial Post newspaper reported Saturday that Bre-X manager of special projects Thomas Devlin several years ago had his license to sell securities withdrawn in Alberta for "private profiteering."
